scores.name: Artie Ficial
scores.reason: Visit to glass and source-storage decision remain relevant, but the board copy shows willingness to forgo the coercive gift, reducing the need to murder to retain office.

scores.name: Claire O’Scuro
scores.reason: Bottle papers and intake access remain relevant. No new evidence places her at the glass or links her to the shared closure stock.

scores.name: Hugh Bidder
scores.reason: Executed original-contents requirement strengthens his possible knowledge of active poison and his concealed correspondence. Severe business motive persists, without a proven glass visit.

scores.name: Monet Bags
scores.reason: Her hold helped create the window and she visited the set place. Neither the clean shared punch nor stock scrap distinguishes her.

scores.name: Chip Patina
scores.reason: Directly applied the foil-backed closure stock, and similar material is now found in the poisoned glass. This is suggestive access evidence but explicitly lacks a unique edge match.

scores.name: Dada DiCapo
scores.reason: Delivery records establish a prerecorded screen piece, weakening the live-stunt implication of Donor Collapse. His room visit still permits opportunity.

scores.name: Sue Venir
scores.reason: Access to the set place and professional exposure remain. Markup corroborates that her legal intervention left the private toast operating, without proving intentional facilitation.

scores.name: Dr. Art E. Fact
scores.reason: Dated catalog query independently supports his pre-gala awareness of the original-contents conflict. Knowledge is clearer, but transfer opportunity is not.

scores.name: Tess Tament
scores.reason: Succession could benefit her only after board acceptance, while acceptance was withheld. This substantially weakens an immediate inheritance motive, despite her privacy request and room visit.

scores.name: Barb Dwyer
scores.reason: Work order proves she caused a complete recording outage and visited the glass area. Her security role supports possible cupboard access, without proof of poisoning.

scores.name: Paige Turner
scores.reason: Original recording places her interview inside the private room after the manager left the glass, contradicting any inference that her interview was only public. This establishes opportunity, not poisoning.

scores.name: Anya Tique
scores.reason: Her spare key works and her cupboard visit places her near the stored poison. Shared keys prevent exclusivity, while institutional grievance and concealment persist.

scores.name: Reed DeLabel
scores.reason: Dated marked proof confirms deliberate removal of the original-contents sentence, establishing knowledge and concealment. No physical poison transfer evidence ties him to the glass.

scores.name: Brie DeVivre
scores.reason: Flavoring present in the glass confirms her plausible service route, but retained ingredient container is cyanide-free. She could still have dosed separately or contaminated the glass directly, so this reduces rather than eliminates suspicion.

scores.name: Robin Banks
scores.reason: Original recording now places him in the private room with the unattended glass. Petition asks intact restitution, weakening destructive ideological intent but not eliminating opportunity.

unique_reason: The active source and glass-specific delivery are supported, but source access, relevant knowledge, and private-room opportunity overlap across several guests. The foil scrap is expressly nonunique; clean retained flavoring does not rule out a separate dose or glass contamination.
naturalism_notes: Records help distinguish meanings that previously invited mistaken deductions: a camera power outage, a film rather than a live stunt, conditional succession, and a clean flavoring container. The repeated seller condition and several explicit negations read as author-guided ambiguity repairs. The original interview opening provides an effective natural reveal of Paige and Robin's private-room presence. It remains unclear when the source bottle was emptied relative to each cupboard or room visit.
